statement.excerpt: I don’t know how we don’t see tens of billions of dollars of write-downs and dead data center debt deals with every investor involved losing every penny, nor do I see how big tech avoids admitting that they wasted all their capex.

from_speaker: tens of billions of dollars of write-downs
every investor involved losing every penny
big tech ... admitting that they wasted all their capex
our_interpretation: Treat the wording as a substantive forecast despite its conversational framing.
Read tens of billions as at least USD 20 billion in aggregate realized AI infrastructure write-downs. The numerical floor is an evaluator interpretation.
Read dead debt deals as defaults or failed restructurings with final losses, rather than lower secondary-market bond prices.
Every investor involved means all investor classes in the failed deals identified as fulfilling the forecast.
Capex refers to the AI buildout discussed in the post, rather than every capital expenditure by technology companies.
Support requires the write-downs, failed deals with total investor losses, and public acknowledgment of wasted AI capex; one component does not establish the whole claim.
criteria.support_condition: Financial statements establish at least USD 20 billion of relevant write-downs, final recovery records show complete losses for every investor class in the qualifying failed deals, and relevant big-tech companies publicly acknowledge that the associated AI capex was wasted.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed resolution of a defined investment cohort establishes that the required losses and admissions did not occur. Recoveries in a particular failed deal contradict total-loss claims about that deal, but do not rule out other qualifying failures in the indefinite future.
